content.overview: Section 15 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 provides the principal penal consequence for contravention of the Act, rules, orders or directions. Whoever fails to comply with or contravenes any provision, or any rule, order or direction under the Act, is punishable with imprisonment or fine or both as the section enacts, with enhanced consequences for continuing contravention. Section 15 is the penalty counterpart to substantive duties under ss. 7, 8 and directions under s. 5.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Contravention of Act/rule/order/direction? (2) Who is the offender (person/company)? (3) Continuing offence? (4) Cognizance path under s. 19?
content.study:
Penalty requires proof of the underlying duty breach. Company liability and continuing-offence structure follow the statutory text — verify current imprisonment/fine figures from the official Act.

No new case invented.

sections.heading: Offence
sections.body: Failure to comply with or contravention of any provision of the Act or any rule made, or order or direction issued under the Act.

sections.heading: Punishment
sections.body: Imprisonment, fine, or both, as enacted; continuing contravention attracts additional daily penalty as the section provides.

sections.heading: Link to duties
sections.body: Common predicates include s. 7 emission/discharge breach, s. 8 hazardous handling breach, and non-compliance with s. 5 directions.

sections.heading: Cognizance
sections.body: s. 19 regulates cognizance of offences under the Act.

sections.heading: Method
sections.body: Prove the specific duty or direction breached, identity of the offender, and any continuing character.

examples.title: Direction breach
examples.body: Unit ignores a written s. 5 closure direction — s. 15 penalty for contravention of direction is attracted, subject to proof and cognizance rules.

hypotheticals.question: Does every environmental harm automatically attract s. 15 without a statutory breach?
hypotheticals.analysis: s. 15 requires failure to comply with or contravention of the Act, rules, orders or directions — not free-standing harm alone.

distinctions.title: s. 15 penalty vs s. 5 directions
distinctions.right: Administrative written directions (including closure) binding the addressee.

misconceptions.trap: s. 15 is the only enforcement tool under the EPA.
misconceptions.correction: s. 5 directions, inspections and sampling operate alongside penal liability under s. 15.
